name: Camilla Massa
who: Captain of Italy's Elite 15 squad; 2023 Hyrox AG (30-34) & Overall World Champion, added a 2025 AG (35-39) title.
why: The clearest window into Italy's Elite 15 push right now, with steady training and race-day content in a scene still building depth.

name: Eugenio Bianchi
who: Italy's Hyrox Pro record holder (55:57), on the Elite 15 roster three seasons running, with a long Spartan Race podium history before switching sports.
why: One of the most-followed Italian Hyrox profiles, bridging an OCR audience into the sport with regular race breakdowns.

name: Fabian Eisenlauer
who: German Elite 15 Doubles athlete who, with partner Jake Williamson, ran the first sub-48-minute Men's Open Doubles time in Hyrox history at Berlin.
why: Open about past struggles with alcohol on the way up, plus sharp doubles-strategy content for a division most creators ignore.

name: Joffrey Voisin
who: France's best-known Hyrox name, a four-time Masters (40+) World Champion who only started racing in his 40s.
why: A late-start comeback story with French-language coaching content that doubles as the entry point for French fans discovering the sport.

name: Jonathon Wynn
who: Australian ex-special-forces soldier and Elite 15 regular, top 10 at three straight World Championships (6th, 9th, 5th).
why: A sobriety-since-2020 story layered on genuine elite results, plus he's outspoken about being passed over for Australia's relay squad.

name: Rebecca Mason
who: The UK's top female Hyrox name for several seasons, a 2022 AG World Champion who raced Elite 15 from 2022 to 2024.
why: A working mum coaching other racers through PRVN while still competing herself — content aimed at everyday athletes, not just the elite bubble.

name: Saskia Millard
who: London A&E doctor who set a European Hyrox Pro record (57:26) just months into her racing career.
why: A near-zero-training-time breakout in a sport that's getting more professionalized by the season — worth watching how far it goes.

name: Gustav Cordua
who: Danish Elite 15 Doubles athlete and graduate engineering student who set the Danish national Pro record (55:29) at home in Copenhagen.
why: A student-athlete balancing a master's degree with Elite 15 racing, with a running doubles storyline alongside partner Sebastian Ifversen.

name: Annie Emilsson
who: Swedish national Pro record holder who broke into the sport's all-time fastest women's times just seven months after her Hyrox debut.
why: One of the fastest rises anywhere in the sport right now — worth following before she's a household name.

name: Agnieszka Maciejewska
who: HYROX Poland ambassador with 13 gold and 4 silver national medals and a 2022 Spartan Race World Championship age-group title.
why: A veteran of Poland's obstacle-racing-to-Hyrox pipeline, now coaching business and personal-effectiveness clients alongside her own racing.

name: Kyle Schoonbee
who: Tokyo 2020 Olympic rower turned South African Hyrox champion, winning Men's Pro at both Cape Town and Johannesburg.
why: An Olympic-caliber engine redirected at Hyrox, in a South African scene that's still young — a genuine crossover story to watch grow.

name: Seena Akbary
who: Dubai-based founder of Energy Camp and 2024 Hyrox Cape Town Champion, now an Under Armour Middle East athlete.
why: By far the biggest following of any Hyrox figure in the Gulf, and a genuine builder of the region's scene rather than just a racer.

name: Maarten Enthoven
who: Dutch engineer and Elite-15-calibre athlete who broke into the all-time Pro men's rankings with a 54:58 win at Hyrox Dublin.
why: Founder of Pro Hyrox Stats — the follow for data-driven breakdowns of the sport as much as for his own racing.

name: Madelyn Eybergen
who: Canadian university cross-country champion turned Hyrox convert — the first Canadian woman under 60 minutes and a Pro 20-24 World Champion.
why: A running pedigree this deep rarely crosses into Hyrox this fast — worth watching as she moves up divisions.

name: Rachael Wade
who: Alabama-based registered dietitian and mother of two who won three straight US Pro races (Houston, Miami, Ottawa) on just 7-8 training hours a week.
why: A genuinely different story than most elite content in this sport: low-volume training, real job, real kids, real wins.

name: Aldo Lozano Marquez
who: Mexican Hyrox ambassador on the Puma Mexico roster with 20-plus podiums racing across Mexico, Brazil, Spain, and the US.
why: The face of HYROX Mexico's ambassador program — the follow for LatAm race coverage and hybrid-performance coaching.

name: Claire Nesbitt
who: Former wine critic turned full-time coach, now a Hyrox Hong Kong ambassador representing HK at the World Championships for a fourth straight year.
why: One of the only dedicated Hyrox voices building the sport specifically for Hong Kong and the wider Asia scene.

name: Araya A. Hargate
who: Thai actress and one of Thailand's most-followed public figures, who completed her Hyrox debut in Women's Doubles at Bangkok 2026.
why: Her debut pulled mainstream Thai press coverage most Hyrox racers never get — the clearest crossover moment the sport has had in Southeast Asia.
